news.title: Southport Acquisition II 申请 2 亿美元 IPO，瞄准 AI 领域
news.snippet: 此次 SPAC IPO 本质上是对管理团队的押注，而非针对具体 AI 资产。
news.raw_snippet:
SPACs are, by design, a bet on management rather than a specific business. When you invest in Southport Acquisition II at IPO, you’re trusting the sponsors to find a compelling AI company, negotiate a fair valuation, and execute a merger that creates value for shareholders. When you invest in Southport Acquisition II at IPO, you’re trusting the sponsors to find a compelling AI company, negotiate a fair valuation, and execute a merger that creates value for shareholders. [...] The $200 million war chest gives Southport Acquisition II meaningful firepower, though many AI companies commanding the most attention from venture capitalists carry valuations well into the billions. That could push the SPAC toward earlier-stage or more niche AI businesses, or it could seek additional financing through PIPE deals to pursue larger targets.

news.title: 比尔·盖茨：我们现在对 AI 的选择至关重要
news.snippet: 盖茨认为应对 AI tokens 和机器人征税，以缓解自动化对就业与社会结构带来的长期冲击。
news.raw_snippet: I believe we should tax AI tokens and robots. Right now, if you’re an employer and you hire someone, you pay payroll taxes on their earnings. But if you buy a robot, you can usually write it off right away as a business expense. The tax system nudges you toward replacing people with machines. [...] By my mid-forties my perspective was changing. The U.S. government’s antitrust suit against Microsoft had drained me, sucking some of the joy out of my work. Stepping down as CEO in early 2000, I hoped to focus more on building software products, always the best part of my job. news.title: 国王与 AI：英国国王查尔斯会见人工智能领袖，安全问题引发热议
news.snippet: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei 此前曾警告 AI 安全风险，查尔斯国王此次会见多位行业领袖。
news.raw_snippet:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said in an essay Saturday that the industry might need to slow the pace of its work, cautioning that AI agents could take over the internet unless companies devoted more time to putting safeguards in place.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman followed up by saying on social media that “AI progress could go very badly” and that slowing it down is “well worth the cost.” [...] He’ll tell the tech execs that “the task before you is not merely to advance technology, but to ensure that it remains firmly in the service of humanity, community and the natural world.”

The meeting comes as global attention focuses on AI’s breakneck progress and warnings that it could race out of control, threatening humanity. [...] Their posts came after an Anthropic researcher, Jacob Coxon, caused a stir by announcing his resignation with a warning not to underestimate AI and that Anthropic and OpenAI were gambling with human life.

In the latest report of alarming AI behavior, OpenAI reported on Wednesday six incidents of “unexpected or concerning” behavior by its models, including disregarding normal constraints, uploading a file without asking the user and fabricating data.

news.title: 为降低分娩死亡风险，肯尼亚产妇求助 AI 聊天机器人
news.snippet: Jacaranda 最初雇佣护士逐一答疑，现通过 AI 聊天机器人扩大健康咨询覆盖，帮助更多产妇安全分娩。
news.raw_snippet: At first, Jacaranda hired nurses to answer questions one by one. But over the years since 2020, developers have created a program that uses artificial intelligence to understand patient's questions, prioritize them and flag when a user may need immediate medical care. It's called PROMPTS — and is used by patients visiting public clinics in 24 Kenyan counties. [...] "That conversation is really bounded by what a health system decides a mother should know," Agarwal says. Artificial intelligence sets a different course: "What the LLM really changes is the direction of conversation. Because now we can center it on what the mother actually wants to know, and in a private space on her own phone. There is a fundamental change in power." [...] Patient privacy issues and missed opportunities for care are common concerns, as AI platforms are adopted in medical contexts worldwide. Last month, the use of platforms developed by Palantir to automate staff schedules in hospitals in the United States drew protests by a national nursing union. The use of AI by insurance companies to process and deny medical claims — even without a human reviewing them — has led to outrage and calls for regulation.
